answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from costly, non-replicable bonding: each agent must lock a scarce staked asset, think of it as a shard of quartz, before it can transact. Fake identities multiply cheaply, but bonded capital does not, so an attacker cloning a thousand agents must fund each one. Honest participants then form a trusted oasis where reputation, earned slowly over real work, acts like a lantern guiding counterparties toward verified peers and away from unbonded swarms.
